Hold the kind and span claims of the install-page pin (#289)

Make the self-checks of tools/test-install-page.py hold what its
docstrings say about the reader pin of check 7, and word those
docstrings so that they claim no more than the checks hold. The gate,
tools/check-install-page.py, is byte identical, so GATE_SHA256 and
READER_SHA256 are unchanged.

- Capture tuple, list and dict when the test is imported, as
  PLAIN_CONTAINERS beside PLAIN_TYPES, and compare the exact type of a
  value with them by identity in plain_data(). Each kind, plain data
  included, is then compared by identity with a type that the test
  captured when it was imported (PLAIN_TYPES, PLAIN_CONTAINERS,
  PIN_KINDS).
- Add capture_problems(): with re.Pattern, types.ModuleType, the
  test's REPO_ROOT, str, bytes, int, float, bool, tuple, list or dict
  rebound to a stand-in, 1 name at a time, pin_value() must still
  write a real value of that kind as before and refuse an instance of
  the stand-in, and each name must be restored once the last of them
  has been rebound. The exact type of a value, and type(None), are
  read with the builtin type(), which a rebinding of a builtin can
  change, a class that the reader pin does not see (residual 2); no
  check holds the capture of type.
- Derive refusal cases from the 3 capture tuples: for each of their 13
  kinds, an object whose class gives the kind as its __class__, and,
  for each of the 10 kinds that FINAL_KINDS does not name, an instance
  of a bare subclass, so that each kind test of pin_value() and
  plain_data() must match the exact type. A subclass that cannot be
  made fails the check, and so does a kind of FINAL_KINDS (bool,
  NoneType and re.Pattern) that Python lets a class subclass. The 19
  committed refused values are kept.
- Run the 2 replacements of REQUESTED_FILES on 3 base gates: the
  committed gate, one in which its statement shares its line with
  LOADED_SEGMENTS and REDIRECT_TARGETS and a comment, and one in which
  it spans 3 lines with a comment after it. Each built gate must first
  pass the reader pin, and each gate with the statement replaced must
  keep the comments of its base gate.
- Make pin_reflowed_gate() refuse an unpacking assignment to
  REQUESTED_FILES, and give both gate builders sources that their
  docstrings refuse, each of which must raise ValueError.
- Rewrite the fixture PIN_SUBCLASS as 1 simple statement with the same
  meaning, a deliberate change of its contract: a class statement
  cannot follow a semicolon, so the committed form does not parse on
  the shared-line gate.
- Add to pin_value()'s docstring that it writes a module, a class or a
  path by its name, so a helper that 1 of them carries is in no
  digest here, and mark its refused values as examples. The pin holds
  the values that a reviewed gate defines in ordinary code, and
  scope_sentence_problems() fails each docstring of the file that says
  so without the words "a module, a class or a path by its name".
- Rewrite the module docstring's account of the kind tests and of
  pin_value_problems() with only what these checks hold.
- Leave .github/squash/269.txt unchanged: this change edits no merged
  squash record.

Checks, each with its expected outcome:

- python3 -I tools/test-install-page.py: exit 0, "all 623 cases".
- python3 -I tools/check-install-page.py: exit 0, and its sha256
  equals GATE_SHA256 before and after this change.
- Each mutant that the description names, 1 or 2 exact replacements
  in a copy of the test: exit 1 with this change, with the problems
  that the description names, and exit 0 on main before this change
  for each mutant whose code main holds.
- python3 -I tools/check-pr-text.py on the description and on this
  message: exit 0, 0 defects.

What TODO 283 records:

- The 5 gaps between the docstrings and the self-checks that the
  review of pull request 269 reported are each closed by a check
  above: the capture of the kinds, the refusal of a subclass of int,
  float or bytes, the capture of tuple, list and dict, the columns of
  the replaced span and the residual of pin_value()'s scope sentence.
  The 2nd is widened to bool and None, the 4th to a span that ends at
  the end of its 1st line and to 1 that takes in a comment after the
  statement, and the 1st to str, bytes, int, float and bool.
- pin_value()'s docstring gives its refused values as examples and
  points to pin_value_problems(), which names the values that it
  holds; every count in this message and the description names its
  unit.
- The fixture PIN_SUBCLASS changes its contract deliberately, for the
  reason above.
- GATE_SHA256 and READER_SHA256 are unchanged.
